name: Phi-4-multimodal

lifecycle.note: Weights remain downloadable from Microsoft's Hugging Face organisation; Microsoft Foundry lists the model as GA without a retirement date (checked 2026-10-01).

sources.locator: Abstract; vision and speech/audio modality sections

relations.note: Uses the pretrained Phi-4-mini-instruct language model as backbone, kept frozen, with added vision and speech encoders, projectors and modality-specific LoRA adapters (mixture of LoRAs).

Editorial link along the Phi multimodal line: the model card presents the release as a response to Phi-3 series feedback, where users had to chain a speech recognition model with the Mini and Vision models, but names no direct predecessor. Phi-3.5-vision was the latest Phi vision model before it.

summary.text: Phi-4-multimodal is a 5.6-billion-parameter model in Microsoft's Phi family that accepts text, image and audio input and produces text, released on 26 February 2025 with Phi-4-mini. It handles all three modalities in one model through a mixture of LoRAs on a Phi-4-mini backbone, and was offered in Azure AI Foundry, the NVIDIA API Catalog and as MIT-licensed open weights.

changes.text: Adds image and audio input to the Phi-4-mini language model, which stays frozen, through vision and speech encoders with LoRA adapters.
Adds speech and audio input; with the Phi-3 series, users had to put a separate speech recognition model in front of the Vision model.
Processes text, vision and speech in a single model with a mixture of LoRAs, without separate pipelines per modality.
Uses a larger vocabulary for multilingual support, with text input in 23 languages; vision input is English only.

notes: Announced and released together with Phi-4-mini. The announcement calls it Microsoft's first multimodal language model; the Phi product page says more precisely that it is the first Phi model that supports text, audio and vision inputs. The successor-of link to Phi-3.5-vision is editorial; on Microsoft Foundry the suggested replacement for the retired Phi-3.5-vision-instruct is Phi-4-mini-instruct, not this model. The vision encoder is based on SigLIP-400M (technical report), a model from another organisation; that link is not recorded here.
